text:
Martin Fehérváry plays 21 minutes a night for Washington, blocks shots by the dozen (51 already, in 18 games) and has spent the first month watching his team miss with him on the ice. The Capitals have scored 7.5 fewer goals than their chances deserved while he plays, which is why he has 4 assists and no goals. That gap usually swings back, and it's the main thing standing between him and a normal points pace.

The process looks better than the box score. Washington has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a real setup man last season, 6.6 primary shot assists per 60, 94th percentile among defensemen, so his passes from the offensive zone are worth watching. He also had 4 points for Slovakia at the 2026 Olympics. Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level last season, though, so the case for him is still more about minutes and defense than about a breakout.
